details.title: Chrome 페이지 메뉴에서 Gemini·검색을 저장·인쇄보다 위에 배치하는 실험
details.summary: 기존 menu-simplification에 glic section above save 옵션을 추가한다. 텍스트 미선택·비편집 페이지 메뉴에서 Gemini·검색 구역을 저장·인쇄 구역 위로 옮긴다. 기능과 새 매개변수의 기본값은 비활성화다.
reasons: 기존 만료 연장과 달리 메뉴 구성 코드의 순서 변경이 확인된다. AI/검색 발견성과 기존 저장·인쇄 과제의 조작 비용을 동일 조건으로 비교할 수 있는 소스 실험이다.
Original priority reason: 메뉴 순서의 제한된 탐색적 비교이며 실제 배포·설치본 노출은 확인되지 않았다.
Imported legacy judgment; no new PM evaluation. Provenance: data/event-revisions/chrome-context-menu-gemini-search-order-source-20261113/schema-v1.json
details.comparison_question: 페이지 메뉴의 Gemini·검색 우선 배치가 AI 진입 발견성과 저장·인쇄 탐색 시간·오선택률을 어떻게 바꾸는가?

evidence.excerpt: On macOS, keyboard shortcuts assigned to Firefox menu items in System Settings now replace the built-in shortcuts for those items.

details.title: On macOS, keyboard shortcuts assigned to Firefox menu items in System Settings now replace the built-in shortcuts for those items.
details.summary: On macOS, keyboard shortcuts assigned to Firefox menu items in System Settings now replace the built-in shortcuts for those items.
reasons: Evidence-gated deterministic profile macos-menu-shortcut-override: macOS users can replace browser menu shortcuts with system preferences. This changes keyboard task completion and shortcut conflicts.
Evidence: On macOS, keyboard shortcuts assigned to Firefox menu items in System Settings now replace the built-in shortcuts for those items.
Material change: The official Beta note says custom shortcuts now replace built-in shortcuts; this is a historical Beta note, not a newly observed launch.

Benchmark: Confirm browser availability and the stated Beta behavior on the same macOS device → Assign a menu shortcut in System Settings → Invoke both the custom and former shortcuts while a page input has focus → Restore the original setting
Measure: Successful menu invocations; Unexpected text input or conflicting commands; Setup steps
Completion: Three repetitions per supported browser; record outcomes and unavailable paths. No execution is claimed.

Conditions: Beta documentation only; no device test. Confirm both browsers and menu support on macOS first. If Samsung Browser is unavailable on macOS, retain as a design comparison and do not report a cross-product performance result.
details.comparison_question: On the same macOS version, can a user override a browser menu shortcut through System Settings, and what happens to the former shortcut in Firefox and Samsung Browser if available?

details.title: Source baseline: Parallel downloading
reasons: Evidence-gated deterministic profile enable-parallel-downloading-benchmark: A download can use parallel transfers. Download completion and recovery are concrete tasks; the source description is a claim to test, not proof of acceleration.
Evidence: Enable parallel downloading to accelerate download speed.

Material change: An active registration is documented at the pinned source baseline. This selects an existing experiment for research; it does not date its introduction or claim a new product release.

Benchmark: Confirm the flag exists in an accessible build and document default state → Serve a synthetic file from a server with range requests → Download with the option enabled and disabled under the same network cap → Repeat after one controlled network interruption and compare the same task in an available Samsung Browser build
Measure: Completion time; Transferred bytes; Recovery success and file hash
Completion: Three repetitions for each supported condition; record setup and failures. No execution is claimed.
Conditions: Source-only baseline; installed availability, rollout and test results are unknown. Confirm platform/build access before executing. Use synthetic data in an approved test environment.
details.comparison_question: For an identical large file and controlled network, how do enabled and disabled parallel downloading affect completion time and recovery, and how does Samsung Browser behave under the same conditions?

details.title: Source baseline: Actor observe screenshot default
details.summary: Source baseline: Actor observe screenshot default
reasons: Evidence-gated deterministic profile actor-observe-screenshot-default-benchmark: An agent framework can capture page screenshots by default when requested. The default capture surface raises a concrete user-control and sensitive-page comparison task.
Evidence: If enabled, the actor framework will capture screenshots by default when requested.

Material change: An active registration is documented at the pinned source baseline. This selects an existing experiment for research; it does not date its introduction or claim a new product release.

Benchmark: Build or obtain an accessible revision with this registration and confirm the actor path is present → Use synthetic pages with visible and off-screen markers → Request observation with the option enabled and disabled → Inspect captured markers and available user controls; compare another browser agent only if it supports the same task
Measure: Captured marker coverage; Capture events per request; User-visible controls and cancellation outcome
Completion: Three repetitions for each supported condition; record setup and failures. No execution is claimed.
Conditions: Source-only baseline; installed availability, rollout and test results are unknown. Confirm platform/build access before executing. Use synthetic data in an approved test environment.
details.comparison_question: In a controlled browser-agent task, what page content enters a screenshot when observation is requested, and can the user inspect or stop that transfer?
